text:
maria: Heads-up — after upgrade to grpc v1.42 we see a host-side CPU bump (~12%) on the tokenization/parse path for short requests. Running a quick perf diff now.
cheng: Can you paste the perf/top lines you saw? was it syscall heavy or pure lib parsing?
maria: quick snapshot from perf script:
```
  samples  %        command  shared_object          symbol
   6120   35.1%     hostd    libc.so.6              __writev
   2100   12.0%     hostd    host_tokenizer.so      tokenize_batch
   1150    6.6%     hostd    grpc_core.so           grpc_call_start_batch
    900    5.2%     hostd    host_parse.so          parse_request
```
maria: Most of the extra samples are in `__writev` and `grpc_call_start_batch` for short chat requests (avg seq_len ~ 24 tokens).
alex: That reeks of smaller writes / lack of writev coalescing after the http2 framing change. grpc -> writev emits many tiny iovecs.
sam: Also seeing more KV cache evictions for these short requests; hotset size dropped. Maybe pre-tokenize -> different keys -> extra cache churn.
raj: Did we change any preparse/pretokenize flags in the client? I remember a toggle was flipped in the shim to reduce memory for large requests.
maria: We flipped `pretokenize_on_ingress: true` in the shim to try to reduce tail latency for long sequences. Turns out it increases syscall overhead for shorts because we pre-tokenize everything then stream.
cheng: Proposed mitigation list:
- coalesce socket writes in the grpc transport for small iovecs (batch small iovs into single writev)
- add a short-request fastpath that skips pretokenize for seq_len < 64
- adjust KV cache keying to use raw request hash for pretokenized-disabled path (reduce churn)
- small-request batching heuristic: when candidate batch size == 1 and seq_len < 64, send through slim kernel (lower kernel selection overhead)
alex: For kernel selection: prefer low-latency fp16 kernels for sequences < 64, avoid the warmup/quantization path that favours throughput.
sam: I ran a quick canary patch locally: disabled pretokenize for seq_len<64 and added coalesce at transport. microbench results (p50/p99 on short chat set):
```
baseline: CPU 100%, p50 24ms, p99 310ms
w/ coalesce + disable-pretokenize: CPU 93%, p50 25ms, p99 260ms
```
sam: CPU down ~7%, p99 improved a lot.
maria: infra-bot kicked canary deploy at 1762123500 — @infra-bot can you paste canary metrics?
infra-bot: Canary results: 30m window, traffic toggled for ingesters-001: short-req QPS 12k
- host_cpu: -6.8%
- p50_lat: +0.5ms
- p99_lat: -18%
- kv_evictions/min: -22%
alex: Nice. That validates both coalesce and cache-key fix. We should do a small change set:
1) add transport coalesce for iovecs < 2KB
2) short-request flag to disable pretokenize
3) kernel selector tweak for seq_len < 64 to prefer low-latency kernel
4) KV cache key normalization for pretokenized disabled path
raj: I'll own (2) and (4). alex you take (1), maria take (3). Sam can own perf verification + dashboard updates.
maria: Opening PR drafts. quick patch snippet for config toggle:
```
# ingress-config.yaml
pretokenize_short_requests: false  # when false, skip pretokenize if seq_len < 64
```
cheng: Also add a metric `ingress.preparse_skipped` so we can measure skippage rate, and `transport.writev_coalesced` to monitor any regression.
sam: I'll add sample queries to the perf dashboard. Recommend rolling this to Dedicated canaries first, then Hosted.
raj: Any reason not to ship this as hotfix to the next patch? It seems low-risk and contained to host-side.
alex: Only concern: turning off pretokenize might slightly increase latency for large requests. But our medians show no regression; we'll gate by seq_len so should be fine.
maria: OK creating PRs targeting the host-runtime branch, will add benchmarks and combined perf diffs. Will tag @eng-sre for rollout plan.
sam: I'll run a 24h smoke with canary toggled in eu-west-1 and post results here.
maria: thanks team. followups: PRs in review, perf dashboard queries, alert for writev_coalesce < 99%.
cheng: 👍
raj: :thumbsup:
